It can already walk, sit, crouch, roller skate, pick up objects with an articulated beak, recover from falls, run autonomous behaviors, and interact with NFC-tagged accessories, making it an unusually capable and inexpensive platform for playful robotics development.

title: GRAFT: Grounded and Efficient Online Reinforcement Adaptation for Fine-Grained Robot Manipulation
summary: GRAFT adapts pretrained vision-language-action robot policies online for fine-grained biomedical manipulation by learning view-specific visual anchors from region-level supervision, so the policy focuses on subtle local cues without needing region proposals at deployment. It also speeds adaptation with single-step action generation and cached visual-language prefixes, improving success across four biomedical tasks by 25 percentage points under the same adaptation budget while reducing update overhead.

extra.full_text: Pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) policies provide strong priors for robot manipulation, yet adapting them online to fine-grained biomedical tasks remains challenging. Task success often hinges on subtle, view-dependent visual cues, while task-level rewards provide little guidance about which regions matter, making it difficult to learn task-relevant visual grounding from limited real-robot interaction. Online adaptation is further constrained by the computational cost of VLA inference and replay-based updates. We introduce GRAFT (Grounded Reinforcement Adaptation for Fast Task Learning), a framework for efficient online VLA adaptation through grounded perception. GRAFT uses region-level supervision to learn view-specific visual anchors that focus perception on task-relevant local cues without requiring region proposals at deployment. It further combines single-step action generation with cached visual-language prefix reuse to accelerate online learning. Across four biomedical manipulation tasks, GRAFT improves success rates by 25 percentage points under matched adaptation budgets, while reducing the computational overhead of online policy updates.

title: Introducing S1: A robot model that learns from one example
summary: Skild AI introduced S1, a robotics foundation model that takes a single video demonstration as a prompt and generates actions for previously unseen, up-to-10-minute tasks without fine-tuning. The company says S1 can generalize across environments and robot embodiments, compose pretrained skills or infer new ones, and handle perturbations rather than replaying the demo verbatim. On novel tasks, Skild claims one prompted example can match what current language-prompted VLA systems would need 50-100 hours of data collection and fine-tuning to achieve.

extra.full_text: Announcing S1, our new foundation model that learns from one example. Summary on X: https://x.com/SkildAI/status/2092300842900865389 Technical blog: https://skild.ai/blogs/s1 S1 can be taught 10-minute long tasks that it has never seen before, from one video prompt without any fine-tuning. How? It learns new tasks like a language model. You prompt it with a video demonstration, and it outputs robot actions to complete the task in any environment and in any embodiment. By composing skills learned in pretraining or creating new ones, it can make coffee, pot a plant, fry pancakes, and more – tasks never seen during pretraining. The first time S1 flipped a pancake, we assumed pancake flipping must have been in its pre-training data. We searched our whole pre-training data of a million hours and found no examples of flipping. S1 inferred the out-of-distribution task from one video prompt. S1 does not blindly replay the video demonstration. Instead, it displays common-sense understanding that goes beyond the video prompt. It can withstand perturbations and improvise upon mistakes, even if the human didn’t. At times, S1 executes with more precision than the human in the video prompt Compared to conventional VLAs, S1 is a step-change improvement. For known tasks, S1 can match the performance of language-prompted VLAs. For novel tasks, S1 exponentially outperforms any existing language-prompted VLAs as we scale the pre-training. We found that to match the accuracy that S1 can achieve with just one example of prompting, current VLA models would need to be post-trained with 50-100 hours of data collection followed by fine-tuning! We believe this is a promising direction towards establishing scaling laws for robotics. We're excited to deploy S1 with our limited industrial partners today, rolling out to more customers over the next few months. S1 is the first light on a new path towards general intelligence grounded in the physical world. skild.ai

extra.full_text: Regulated industries require full ownership,control and customization of the models they deploy with end-to-end governance, transparency, and auditability. This livestream explores how Domyn has built and specialized its own models, including a 263B-parameter reasoning model purpose-built for regulated industries and smaller models for specific domains and tasks. We'll walk through the training pipeline: model compression, multilingual continual pretraining, supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, leveraging the NVIDIA open source ecosystem. Learn how this approach delivers state-of-the-art results on enterprise tasks like text-to-SQL, knowledge graph extraction, and safety classification, and enable AI that you can own, control and customize, built for the demands of regulated industries.

title: “AI가 이제 현실 세계를 움직인다”…앤트로픽, '모델 하드웨어 표준(MHS)’ 프리뷰 공개
summary: Anthropic previewed the Model Hardware Standard, a proposed interface for AI agents to connect to and control physical lab and manufacturing equipment in a standardized way. The initial release is limited to science labs and advanced manufacturers, where Anthropic plans to work with early partners on safety evaluations and usage guidelines before broader deployment.

extra.full_text: 앤트로픽(Anthropic)이 인공지능(AI) 에이전트가 실제 로봇 등 물리적 장비 및 기기를 안전하게 제어할 수 있도록 하는 새로운 하드웨어 표준을 선보였다.앤트로픽은 27일(현지시간) AI 에이전트가 연구실과 제조 현장의 다양한 장비를 표준 방식으로 연결하고 제어할 수 있도록 설계한 ‘모델 하드웨어 표준(Model Hardware Standard, MHS)’의 연구 프리뷰를 공개했다.MHS는 우선 과학 연구소와 첨단 제조업체를 대상으로 제한적으로 제공된다. 앤트로픽은 초기 파트너들과 함께 안전성 평가와 활용 가이드라인을 마련한
